draft.title: Molecules and compounds
card: two or more atoms joined together. The atoms can be the same kind or different kinds.
a substance with two or more different elements chemically joined. The elements are joined in fixed amounts.
A compound has properties unlike the elements it is made from. Sodium is a soft metal and chlorine is a poisonous gas, but sodium chloride is the salt we put on chips.
Oxygen gas is a molecule made of two oxygen atoms, but it is not a compound because it has only one element. Water is both a molecule and a compound.
draft.remember: A compound joins different elements in fixed amounts, and it behaves differently from them.

opts: Water, made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms joined
Oxygen gas, made of two oxygen atoms joined
Helium gas, made of single helium atoms
Iron, made of iron atoms only
a.why: Water has two different elements, hydrogen and oxygen, chemically joined, so it is a compound. Oxygen gas is a molecule, but both its atoms are the same, so it has only one element.
a.clue: A compound needs more than one kind of element.

b.q: Priya says that carbon dioxide is a compound because it is a molecule. Which reason shows what is wrong with her reasoning?
opts: Some molecules have only one element, so are not compounds
Some compounds have only one atom, so are not molecules
Molecules never have properties unlike their atoms
Molecules are always made of atoms of different elements
b.why: A molecule is two or more atoms joined, and they can be the same kind, as in oxygen gas. So being a molecule does not make something a compound. Carbon dioxide is a compound because it has two different elements, carbon and oxygen, joined.
b.clue: Think about oxygen gas, which has two atoms joined.

a.best: Water, made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms joined

b.best: Some molecules have only one element, so are not compounds

problems.detail: Both distractors that are plainly false use absolutes ('always', 'never'). The card says atoms 'can' be the same or different kinds. A test-wise student can rule those two out without knowing the idea, which leaves a 50/50 between the two 'Some' options.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. In question b, two distractors use 'always' and 'never', which lets students eliminate them by test-taking habit rather than understanding.
